newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Hochtief sees 1996 profits lower.
newsitem.headline: German Hochtief sees 1996 profits lower.

text.p: FRANKFURT, Nov 29 Reuter) - Hochtief AG, Germany's second largest building group, said on Friday it expected 1996 profits not quite to reach those in 1995 because of the weak overall German market and the cost of its restructuring measures.
"As a whole we must assume that we shall not quite reach the net result shown in the previous year," the company said in a report to employees.
Hochtief had previously given no precise forecast for the 1996 year except to say that it was hopeful of profit "continuity" in relation to the net profit of 137 million marks it made in 1995.

The report by the Hochtief board over the first nine-months of the year said that it was clear that continued strength in its international business would not be able fully to offset the fall in its domestic profits.

The profit warning came despite figures in the report showing an 11.1 percent rise in nine-month building output to 8.82 billion marks, helped by a 28.5 percent gain in international output to 3.52 billion marks.
Incoming orders were 44.3 percent above the previous-year level at 11.8 billion marks, again helped by a large gain in international activity, where orders rose 94 percent to six billion marks.

Separately, a Hochtief spokeswoman confirmed a newspaper report that the company was interested in pursuing "cooperation" possibilities with former takeover target Holzmann, where it has a 20 percent stake.
Hochtief is currently seeking to overturn a German cartel office ruling preventing it from increasing its stake for competition reasons.
